title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report details verified findings on 220 support tickets, revealing a total labor cost of $17,445.07 and an average resolution time of 75.7 minutes. Analysis indicates that the Beta team incurs the highest labor costs, while email tickets show a significantly higher reopening rate compared to chat. A small segment of high-cost, low-satisfaction tickets was identified, and agent workload is relatively distributed with no single agent dominating the volume.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 220 tickets with a total labor cost of $17,445.07 and a mean resolution time of 75.66 minutes.
Team Beta has the highest total labor cost at $6,928.72, followed by Gamma ($5,911.44) and Alpha ($4,604.91).
Chat channels have the longest mean resolution time at 82.23 minutes, followed by phone (74.07 minutes) and email (71.72 minutes).
The email reopening rate is 15.24%, which is 122.48% higher than the chat reopening rate of 6.85%.
There are 9 tickets classified as high-cost and low-satisfaction, representing a segment with an 11.11% reopening rate.
Resolution times have a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.3 minutes. The mean satisfaction score is 4.14, with 14 missing satisfaction records.
Tickets are handled by 18 unique agents. The most active agent handled 16 tickets, accounting for 7.27% of the total volume.

limitations: The cleaning and analysis stages reported validation failures, suggesting potential data quality issues in the source exports.
Satisfaction scores were missing for 14 tickets, which may bias the calculated mean satisfaction score.
The analysis assumes labor cost is directly aggregable and does not account for hourly rate variations per agent.
conclusion: The support operations data highlights significant efficiency variances, particularly the high reopening rate for email tickets compared to chat. While agent workload appears balanced, the identified high-cost, low-satisfaction segment warrants further investigation to reduce operational risk. Addressing the specific drivers of email reopenings could yield substantial quality improvements.
